cards.f: Four levels of response in long answers
cards.b: Knowledge, application, analysis, evaluation. Top marks need a justified judgement.
Knowledge: correct but generic points. Application: points linked to the case business, using its facts and figures.
A developed chain of reasoning: point, because, which means, effect on the business.
A clear decision or judgement, justified with case evidence and compared with the alternatives.
Give a short answer with no explanation.
Give the precise meaning of a term.
Set out the main points briefly (point plus brief development).
Work out from the data; show working and give units.
Give reasons; say why or how, with supporting detail.
Make a decision and support it with evidence, explaining why it is better than the alternatives.
Read the questions first, then the case; underline business type, legal form, objectives, problems; note the key fact in each appendix.
Point (K) → Apply to the case (App) → Develop the consequence (An).
Each option: one advantage and one disadvantage applied to the case. Then a decision paragraph: why best, why others are worse, what it depends on.
About 1 mark per minute after reading; 8 marks ≈ 8–9 min, 12 marks ≈ 14–15 min. Always write the decision paragraph.
This means that…, As a result…, This leads to…, Therefore…, Because… Each moves the chain one step towards an outcome.

gaps.s: Using the facts and figures of the case study business in your answer is called ___ .
A developed chain of cause and effect reasoning is called ___ .
A justified judgement that weighs up alternatives is ___ .
The command word ___ means give the precise meaning of a term.
In a 'justify' answer you must make a clear ___ .
The Explain structure is point, apply, then develop the ___ .
You should read the ___ first, before the case study.
An answer that is correct but could apply to any business reaches only the ___ level.

short.q: State two ways of showing application in a case study answer. [2]
short.model: Use the business's name, products or workers, and quote or calculate with figures from the appendix.
points: use case facts such as name/product

short.q: Explain why a list of advantages and disadvantages with no development scores few marks. [3]
short.model: Lists show only knowledge. Analysis marks need a chain of reasoning explaining the effect on the business.

short.q: A 12-mark question asks you to recommend one of three options. Outline how to structure the answer. [4]
short.model: Consider one advantage and one disadvantage of each option, applied to the case. Then write a decision paragraph saying which is best, why the others are worse and what it depends on.
points: each option with advantage and disadvantage

short.q: Explain why a recommendation that only repeats earlier points does not earn evaluation marks. [2]
short.model: Evaluation needs a justified judgement that compares alternatives with case evidence. Repeating points does not show why the choice is better.

short.q: Describe how you should use your reading time on a Paper 2 case study. [3]
short.model: Read the questions first, then the case, underlining key facts. Note what each appendix shows and do any calculations needed.
